title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection sensitivity and add hysteresis rollout guard
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Recent canary runs showed repeated small latency regressions that briefly triggered rollouts and then recovered, leading to unnecessary rollbacks and customer noise. This PR tightens the auto-detection sensitivity for low-SNR regressions and adds hysteresis-based rollout guards to prevent flip-flopping during transient noise. What changed: 1) Detection algorithm: adjust threshold computation to use trimmed-mean latency with dynamic confidence intervals instead of simple percentile deltas; this reduces sensitivity to outliers while preserving fast detection of sustained regressions. 2) Hysteresis guard: introduce a two-stage state machine (normal -> alerted -> triggered) with configurable hold-down and decay windows; only after N consecutive alert windows does the canary status escalate to triggered. When metrics trend back below threshold we decay the alert count over a longer period to prevent immediate re-triggering. 3) Config surface: new fields in canary-config.yaml: detection.trim_pct, detection.confidence_multiplier, hysteresis.alert_windows, hysteresis.decay_windows. 4) Telemetry: add new metrics perf_canary.hysteresis_state, perf_canary.trimmed_mean_latency and perf_canary.alert_window_count. 5) Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for detector logic, integration canary harness test using synthetic workloads, and a perf replay with real canary traces to validate no-loss detection latency for regressions >10% sustained for 3 windows. Rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary cluster with dark launch for 48 hours, observe false-positive rate and time-to-detection on historical traces, then enable guard for all canaries. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - detector and hysteresis - [x] Integration canary harness run - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Docs: config flags documented - [x] Release notes included Notes: tuned defaults are conservative: alert_windows=3, decay_windows=6, trim_pct=0.1, confidence_multiplier=1.5. These were chosen based on 6 months of canary traces to balance sensitivity and noise tolerance. If needed, defaults can be changed via cluster config.

short_description: Adjust canary detection to use trimmed mean, add hysteresis guard to avoid transient flip-flops, add telemetry and tests.
notes_for_release: Dark-launch for 48 hours before global enable

detection:

rationale: Empirical analysis of 6 months of canary traces showed that trimmed-mean reduced false positives caused by outliers while keeping detection latency for sustained regressions acceptable. Hysteresis prevents repeated rollouts on transient noise.
